question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 62° more than the smaller one. The smaller angle (in degree) is:
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Sum of two **supplementary angles** = 180° Difference between the angles = 62° **Smaller angle** = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 **Smaller angle** = (180° − 62°) ÷ 2 = 118° ÷ 2 = 59° **∴ The correct answer is 59°.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:** Larger angle = Smaller angle + 62° Sum of **supplementary angles** = 180° **Formula Used:** If two angles are supplementary, their sum is 180°. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9abeca962921169dc2204c6e747fe9d4b73528d71b0928b066bddc4605602e8.png] **Calculations:** ⇒ Let the **smaller angle** be x. ⇒ Then the **larger angle** = x + 62°. ⇒ Since they are **supplementary**, x + (x + 62°) = 180° ⇒ 2x + 62° = 180° ⇒ 2x = 180° − 62° ⇒ 2x = 118° ⇒ x = 59° **∴ The correct answer is 59°.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
